cards.label: 01 · §20.20 Production
cards.title: Producing elliptically polarised light
cards.body: A polariser and a quarter-wave plate (QWP) turn unpolarised light into elliptically polarised light.
points: Polariser: unpolarised light becomes plane polarised light.
QWP: set E to the optic axis at \(\theta \neq 45^\circ\).
Rays: the o-ray and e-ray get amplitudes \(E\sin\theta\) and \(E\cos\theta\).
Exit: path difference \(\lambda/4\) (phase \(90^\circ\)) gives elliptical light.

cards.label: 02 · §20.20.1 Detection
cards.title: Detecting elliptically polarised light
cards.body: An analyser shows elliptical light; a QWP placed before it separates it from partially polarised light.
points: Analyser: intensity varies from max to min, never zero.
Same result for partially polarised light, so a QWP is needed.
QWP first: the analyser extinguishes the beam twice per rotation.
The QWP adds \(90^\circ\), the total is \(180^\circ\), and the output is plane polarised.

cards.label: 03 · §20.21 Production
cards.title: Producing circularly polarised light
cards.body: A polariser and a QWP turn unpolarised light into circularly polarised light when E is at 45°.
points: Polariser: unpolarised light becomes plane polarised light.
QWP: rotate the polariser and QWP so E is at \(45^\circ\) to the optic axis.
Rays: the o-ray and e-ray have equal amplitudes.
Exit: path difference \(\lambda/4\) (phase \(90^\circ\)) gives circular light.

cards.label: 04 · §20.21.1 Detection
cards.title: Detecting circularly polarised light
cards.body: An analyser alone cannot separate circular light from unpolarised light; a QWP placed before it can.
points: Analyser: intensity stays uniform on rotation.
Same result for unpolarised light, so a QWP is needed.
QWP first: the analyser extinguishes the beam completely twice per rotation.
No extinction after the QWP: the light is unpolarised.

cards.label: 05 · §20.22 Analysis
cards.title: Step 1: rotate a polariser on the unknown light
cards.body: The first full rotation sorts the beam into one of three groups.
points: Two extinctions per rotation: plane polarised. Stop here.
Max and min, never zero: elliptical or partially polarised.
Constant intensity: circular or unpolarised.

cards.label: 06 · §20.22 Analysis
cards.title: Step 2: QWP first, then the polariser
cards.body: For the two undecided groups, the QWP goes before the polariser and the polariser is rotated again.
points: Elliptical: QWP gives plane light; the polariser extinguishes it twice.
Partially polarised: max and min, never zero, after the QWP.
Circular: QWP gives plane light; the polariser extinguishes it completely twice.
Unpolarised: intensity stays constant after the QWP.

cards.label: Relation
cards.title: Amplitudes set the polarisation state
points: Elliptical: \(\theta \neq 45^\circ\), so the two amplitudes differ.
Circular: \(\theta = 45^\circ\), so \(E_o = E_e\).
Both cases: path difference \(\lambda/4\), phase difference \(90^\circ\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: On rotating a polariser, the intensity stays constant. The light is:
cards.why: Constant intensity on rotation means circular or unpolarised light; a QWP separates them.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: Intensity varies from max to min, never zero, on rotation. The light is:
cards.why: Minima that never reach zero rule out plane light; the light is elliptical or partial.

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: Circular light with a QWP before the analyser gives ______ extinctions per rotation.
cards.why: The QWP makes the circular light plane polarised, which the analyser extinguishes twice.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: For circular light, what angle (degrees) does E make with the QWP optic axis?
cards.why: Equal o-ray and e-ray amplitudes need E at 45° to the optic axis.
